description: Raw mouse input with no acceleration and no smoothing (B0001, B0002), from black-ops-2-decomp's P0002. A thread of its own reads the mouse's raw input (WM_INPUT, device counts, 64-bit counters), so Windows' pointer speed and acceleration, the screen edges and the frame rate no longer change how far the view turns, and high polling rates cost the game nothing; menus keep the cursor. cl_mouseAccel and m_filter have no effect (the remote-control view too). If Windows refuses raw input registration, the game stops with an error naming the Windows error code; there is no fallback to the cursor. Store build, loaded into the game by runtime/loader (docs/enhanced-build.md).
tests: tests/enhanced/test_mouse.py: IN_Frame is the original where the raw counts equal the cursor's movement and gives CL_MouseEvent the counts otherwise; a failed registration is a fatal error; the counters add relative reports while the game is in front, take, reset and clamp; CL_GetMouseMovementWithSensitivity is the original without cl_mouseAccel and m_filter; cl_mouseAccel and m_filter change nothing in CL_MouseMove; the loader's jumps reach the replacements. tools/runtime_link.py: no trap reachable from the replacements

description: Mouse sensitivity in MW2019's units (B0003, B0004), from black-ops-2-decomp's P0003: m_sens (default 1.5, 0.01 to 100, archived, registered on first use) turns the view by m_sens * 0.0066 degrees per count at any field of view, hip fire and aiming down sights alike; the sensitivity dvar, the FOV scale and m_yaw no longer apply to the mouse, m_pitch's sign still inverts (0 stops the pitch). The view angles are kept in double precision between frames, and the yaw is kept within [-180, 180). Strafing and forward moves by the mouse use the counts as the original would at sensitivity m_sens * 0.3.

description: BO2-style local GDK bootstrap: resolve only the enhanced DLL and initialize the local game-directory path; all interfaces are rejected and outputs cleared. No system runtime or authorization is invoked. Legacy providers remain unreachable through this boundary; features requiring authorization may fail.

No Xbox Live HTTP: the Xbox services library's HTTP provider is created without starting XCurl, and every request returns E_HC_NO_NETWORK at once, so achievements, presence and social calls behave as offline and nothing is sent (docs/online.md).
Keep the local engine task groups initialized when Xbox Live is unavailable. Bootstrap uses the process-local runtime and leaves platform queues, accounts, and Store entitlements unavailable.
The DemonWare resolver reports zero addresses before calling Winsock, matching the BO2 default. The engine retains its own address parser for local networking.
